# Data Description

Three data sources feed the analysis: Chicago taxi trip records, hourly weather, and OpenStreetMap points of interest.
Together they cover demand, environmental context, and urban structure.
Full data dictionaries are in @sec-app-data.

## Taxi Trip Data

Downloaded from the Chicago Data Portal on 10 May 2026, the dataset holds every recorded taxi trip from January 2024 to early May 2026: **14,985,679 trips** across 21 columns, extended by seven derived temporal features at load time.

Three portal design choices matter downstream.
Driver and trip IDs are SHA-1 hashes, so there's no personally identifiable information.
All timestamps are rounded to the nearest 15 minutes for privacy, which caps temporal precision but doesn't affect hourly or 4-hourly aggregation.
And location is reported only at census-tract level.
With roughly 800 tracts in Chicago the spatial grain is coarser than GPS, but each tract's centroid coordinates support spatial joins.

## Weather Data

Hourly weather comes from the Open-Meteo Historical Archive API [@openmeteo] over the same date range.
Chicago spans about 600 km² with real microclimatic differences between the lakefront, the urban core, and the far northwest, so a single weather station won't represent it.
We defined three weather zones by K-means clustering on all pickup coordinates, placing zone centroids where demand is densest: the downtown core, O'Hare, and the South Side.
The result is **61,335 hourly observations** (~20,445 per zone) across nine variables.
Temperatures range from $-26.8$ °C to 36.3 °C, with apparent lows of $-32.9$ °C from wind chill.
That's Chicago's continental climate at work, and a plausible driver of taxi demand.

## Point-of-Interest Data

POI data comes from OpenStreetMap via `osmnx` [@boeing2017osmnx].
Raw tags (restaurant, bus_stop, hospital, ...) are too fine-grained and overlapping to use directly, so we collapsed them into seven demand-relevant categories, from food & nightlife (5,640 locations) down to transport (135), leaving **9,124 POIs** after reducing polygons to centroids.
POIs are static: they don't vary over time and aren't counted as demand.
Aggregated per hexagon as category counts, they proxy how strongly each cell attracts trips.
